6192.stem:
The diagram shown is the result of a compass radial survey.

\exfigure{2839_q4b_1}

figures.cap: compass radial survey with points A, B, C, D, E around P

parts.latex: Find the size of angle $BPC$.
Find the distance $BC$, giving your final answer correct to the nearest metre.

solutions.latex:
The bearings from $P$ are $325^\circ$ and $040^\circ$.
$$\angle BPC = 360^\circ - 325^\circ + 40^\circ = 75^\circ$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Which bearing belongs to B or C was not checked against the figure.

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule in triangle $BPC$:
$$\begin{aligned}p^2 &= b^2+c^2-2bc\cos P \\ BC^2 &= 48^2+37^2-2\times 48\times 37\times\cos 75^\circ \\ &= 2753.67\ldots \\ BC &= 52.475\ldots \\ &= 52 \text{ m (to the nearest metre)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit
Writes the cosine rule or uses $\angle BPC = 75^\circ$, or equivalent merit

Round 1 used the true bearing directions, which moved the drawing too far from the paper, so round 2 went back to the crop's geometry. The crop's angles are within about 5° of the stated bearings. N arrow and filled Latex heads (rule 4). The bold 'm' in some lengths is printed as normal text. Labels are \scriptsize, placed to clear every line (rules 2, 11).

solutions.latex:
Use the area formula for a triangle with two sides and the included angle.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area}_{\triangle AOB} &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 85 \times 80 \times \sin(140^\circ - 45^\circ) \\ &\approx 3387 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is D.

6547.stem:
A compass radial survey for block of land ABCD, is shown in the diagram below.

\exfigure{819_q29_1}

figures.cap: compass radial survey of ABCD

parts.latex: Calculate the size of angle AOD.
Calculate the distance along the boundary of the land from A to D, correct to the nearest metre.

solutions.latex:
The bearing of $A$ from $O$ is $045^\circ$ and the bearing of $D$ from $O$ is $318^\circ$.

$$318^\circ - 45^\circ = 273^\circ$$
This is greater than $180^\circ$, so the angle inside the block is

$$\angle AOD = 360^\circ - 273^\circ = 87^\circ$$

In $\triangle AOD$, $OA = 140$ m, $OD = 290$ m and $\angle AOD = 87^\circ$. Use the cosine rule to find the side $AD$ opposite the known angle.

$$\begin{aligned} AD^2 &= 140^2 + 290^2 - 2\times 140\times 290\times \cos 87^\circ \\ &\approx 103\,700 - 4249.68 \\ &\approx 99\,450.3 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} AD &\approx \sqrt{99\,450.3} \\ &\approx 315.4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ AD \approx 315 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

819_q29_1.notes: Radial survey at crop positions: O, A, B, C, D, rays extended collinearly through each point to arrowheads with bearings 318, 045, 125, 215 deg, N arrow, quadrilateral ABCD, distances rotated along their rays and clear of lines (rules 6a, 11, 12). Point letters in maths italic (rule 19). Round 2 fixed 215 deg, B and 045 deg label positions.

figures.cap: compass radial survey of field ABCD from O
solution diagram (drawn by Claude)

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{825_q23_s1}

The bearings of $A$ and $B$ from $O$ are $310^\circ$ and $021^\circ$. Measuring through north, the angle between $OA$ and north is $360^\circ - 310^\circ = 50^\circ$, and the angle between north and $OB$ is $21^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle AOB &= 50^\circ + 21^\circ \\ &= 71^\circ \end{aligned}$$
Use the area of a triangle formula $A = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ with $OA = 75$ and $OB = 60$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 75 \times 60 \times \sin 71^\circ \\ &\approx 2127.4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Area of } AOB \approx 2127 \text{ m}^2$$

825_q23_1.notes: Radial survey quadrilateral ABCD with radials from O, N arrow, bearings and lengths, NOT TO SCALE note, all placed from the crop's pixels. Lines are 0.6pt black, the N arrow has the filled Latex head, labels are in maths italic (rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 11, 19).

825_q23_s1.notes: New sketch. O is at the origin with a north arrow; OA = 75 m on bearing 310 and OB = 60 m on bearing 021, drawn to scale, with triangle side AB. The arcs are 50 degrees (N to OA), 21 degrees (N to OB, larger radius because the angle is small) and 71 degrees for angle AOB (outer arc, value inside). Side lengths are centred outside their sides. Rules 11, 14, 22 applied. 6837.stem:
The diagram shows the results of a radial survey of an area of land.

figures.cap: radial survey with points P, Q, R, S and bearings from O

parts.latex: Show the size of $\angle POQ$ is $100^\circ$.
Calculate the length of $PQ$, correct to the nearest metre.
What is the size of the triangular area $ROQ$, correct to 1 decimal place?

solutions.latex:
$P$ is on a bearing of $340^\circ$ and $Q$ on $080^\circ$. Measured through north, the angle from $OP$ to north is $360^\circ - 340^\circ = 20^\circ$, and from north to $OQ$ is $80^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle POQ &= 20^\circ + 80^\circ \\ &= 100^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.self_check: Bearings 340 and 080 differ by 100 through north.

solutions.latex:
In triangle $POQ$, $OP = 55$, $OQ = 30$ and $\angle POQ = 100^\circ$. Using the cosine rule:
$$\begin{aligned} PQ^2 &= 55^2 + 30^2 - 2 \times 55 \times 30 \times \cos 100^\circ \\ &\approx 4498.0 \\ PQ &\approx 67.07 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ PQ \approx 67 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The bearings of $Q$ and $R$ are $080^\circ$ and $160^\circ$, so
$$\angle ROQ = 160^\circ - 80^\circ = 80^\circ$$
Using the area formula for a triangle with $OQ = 30$ and $OR = 40$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 30 \times 40 \times \sin 80^\circ \\ &\approx 590.9 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

2837_q7_1.notes: Radial survey: the North arrow and the rays to P, Q, S, R are at the crop's directions and lengths (NOT TO SCALE: the crop's angles are kept, not the true bearings, rule 1). The low score comes from label placement: after round 2 some labels are still about 10–25 px out. '40 m' is about 20 px too low, 'NOT TO SCALE' about 50 px too far left with slightly looser line spacing, and 'Q 080°' and '30 m' are a little left. I stopped at the 2-round limit. Reviewer: please check the label positions; no label touches a line.

parts.latex:
The diagram shows part of the information obtained from a radial survey of a block of land. All linear measurements shown are in metres and three of the four corner points of the block are described using bearings taken from point $O$.

\exfigure{495_q18_1}

The boundary from $D$ to $A$ was measured to be 17.1 metres in length.

By first calculating the length of $AD$, determine the bearing of $D$ from $O$.

Give your answer correct to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
Apply the cosine rule in $\triangle DOA$ (sides $OD=13$, $OA=15$, $AD=17.1$) to find $\angle DOA$:
$$\begin{aligned} \cos\angle DOA &= \dfrac{13^2+15^2-17.1^2}{2\times 13\times 15} \\ &= 0.2604871795\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\angle DOA = 74^\circ 54' 3.7'' \approx 75^\circ$$
The difference between the bearings is:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle DOA-\angle DAO &= 75-50 \\ &= 25^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing of } D &= 360-25 \\ &= 335^\circ\text{T} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds $\angle DOA$ and the bearing difference, or equivalent merit
Substitutes into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Source wrote $\angle DOA-\angle DAO=75-50$ with $\angle DAO$ presumably meaning the bearing of $A$ from $O$ (50°); kept as in source, check against the figure. Source does not show an AD length calculation beyond the given 17.1 m; diagram 495_q18_s1 may be wanted.

495_q18_1.notes: Radial survey quadrilateral ABCD with radials from O, the N arrow, lengths 13/14/15/16, the bearings next to A, B and C, and NOT TO SCALE in bold. The positions match the crop (sketch, not to scale; rule 1). The N arrow is a 0.6pt line with a filled Latex head; the scan's heavy stroke was not copied (rules 3, 4). The dashed look of the scan's outer edges is print noise, so they are drawn solid.

parts.latex: Show that $\angle COA = 120^\circ$
Determine the area of $\triangle COA$. Give your answer correct to the nearest square metre.
What is the bearing of A from O?

solutions.latex:
In $\triangle COA$, use the cosine rule with the three known sides:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{25^2 + 15^2 - 35^2}{2 \times 25 \times 15}$$
$$\cos\theta = -\dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\therefore\ \theta = 120^\circ$$

Using the area formula for a triangle,
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 25 \times 15 \times \sin 120^\circ \\ &\approx 162 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct substitution into the area formula, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex: $$\therefore\ \text{the bearing of A from O is } 070^\circ \text{ or } \text{N}70^\circ\text{E}$$

parts.latex: Use the Cosine rule to determine the distance between S and R of the carpark.
If angle $TPQ$ is $80^\circ$, what is the bearing of $T$ from $P$?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{235_q28_s1}

The bearings of $S$ and $R$ from $P$ are $260^\circ$ and $140^\circ$, so the angle between $PS$ and $PR$ is
$$\angle SPR = 260^\circ - 140^\circ = 120^\circ$$
In triangle $PSR$, $PS = 25$ and $PR = 40$. Using the cosine rule, $SR^2 = PS^2 + PR^2 - 2\cdot PS\cdot PR\cos\angle SPR$:
$$\begin{aligned} SR^2 &= 25^2 + 40^2 - 2\times 25\times 40\times\cos 120^\circ \\ &= 625 + 1600 + 1000 \\ &= 3225 \\ SR &= \sqrt{3225} \approx 56.8 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ SR \approx 56.8 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: Written by us; no source solution.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{235_q28_s2}

The bearing of $Q$ from $P$ is $065^\circ$. Since $T$ lies on the other side of north from $Q$, going anticlockwise from $PQ$ by $\angle TPQ = 80^\circ$ gives the direction of $PT$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{bearing of } T &= 065^\circ - 80^\circ \\ &= -15^\circ \\ &= 345^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the bearing of } T \text{ from } P \text{ is } 345^\circ$$

meta.self_check: T is to the upper left of north in the figure, so bearing between 270 and 360; 345 consistent

parts.latex: Use the cosine rule to calculate the length of the remaining boundary $AB$.

solutions.latex:
Bearings of $OA$ and $OB$ from $O$ are $257^\circ$ and $332^\circ$, so

$$\angle AOB = 332^\circ - 257^\circ = 75^\circ$$

Using the cosine rule in $\triangle AOB$ with $OA = 32.4$ and $OB = 28.5$:

$$\begin{aligned} AB^2 &= 32.4^2 + 28.5^2 - 2(32.4)(28.5)\cos 75^\circ \\ AB &\approx 37.2 \text{ km} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds $\angle AOB = 75^\circ$, or substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex: $$\begin{aligned} \text{Perimeter} &= AB + BC + CD + DE + EA \\ &= 37.2 + 36.5 + 38.3 + 40.5 + 34.5 \\ &\approx 187.0 \text{ km} \end{aligned}$$
